task: Corroborate Zetrix AI (ex-MyEG) development-cost and debt figures from independent sources
claim_origin: The Edge Malaysia Weekly, 14-20 Sep 2026 (Cover Story: 'Questions abound about Zetrix AI')
method: Google News RSS (en-MY) query rotation -> outlet site fetches (themalaysianreserve.com, freemalaysiatoday.com) -> full-text figure scan

sources_fetched_full_text.title: Zetrix's billion-ringgit profit paradox
sources_fetched_full_text.author: Rupinder Singh
sources_fetched_full_text.type: Independent weekly business outlet; explicitly flags MARC Ratings as its data source for the asset/borrowings ratios. States 'This article first appeared in The Malaysian Reserve weekly print edition'.

sources_fetched_full_text.title: Perfect storm pushes Zetrix to the precipice
sources_fetched_full_text.type: Independent news outlet (opinion/analysis piece); quotes MBSB Research, MARC, CLSA notes.

sources_fetched_full_text.title: MARC Ratings raises red flag over Zetrix AI's governance
sources_fetched_full_text.url: https://www.nst.com.my (via Google News RSS; article URL not resolved)
sources_fetched_full_text.type: Independent national daily; headline corroborates MARC governance action, not specific figures.

sources_fetched_full_text.title: MARC Slashes Zetrix AI's RM2 Billion Sukuk Rating To BB+, Questions Nasdaq Listing Plans
sources_fetched_full_text.type: Independent outlet; corroborates existence/size of RM2b sukuk programme and MARC downgrade timeline.

titles: Cover Story 1: Questions abound about Zetrix AI (24 Sep)
Frankly Speaking: Zetrix AI must explain the RM3.7 bil development cost (21 Sep)
MARC cuts Zetrix AI sukuk rating... (30 Oct)
sources_fetched_full_text.type: Same-group follow-up coverage - RESTATED, not independent corroboration.

figures.detail: S1: 'cumulative development expenditure had reached approximately RM3.7 billion, compared to RM2.85 billion at end-2025'. S2: 'RM3.7 billion from RM2.85 billion at end-2025'. Two independent outlets give RM2.85b, consistent with The Edge's rounded RM2.8B (note: sources say RM2.85b, not RM2.8b).

S1 and S2 both state approximately RM3.7b cumulative development expenditure at end-June 2026. Also echoed in The Edge's own follow-up headline ('must explain the RM3.7 bil development cost'), restated by S1/S2 independently.
No fetched source gives the FY2020 baseline. Would require the audited FY2020 annual report / Bursa filing.

figures.figure: Development cost exceeds 50% of total assets (key audit matter)
figures.detail: S1 cites MARC Ratings: 'development expenditure represented 56% of Zetrix's total assets' - consistent with, and more precise than, 'exceeds 50%'. The 'key audit matter' characterisation was NOT found in any fetched source; unverified against the actual audit report.

figures.figure: Average RM720.17M/yr development spend over three financial years
figures.detail: Derived figure (implied by RM2.8b->RM3.7b growth plus earlier base); no source states it. Arithmetically consistent with the corroborated end-2025 and end-Jun-2026 values only under The Edge's own derivation.

figures.figure: Only RM28.51M/yr amortised; total amortisation 2020-2025 only RM139.9M
figures.detail: No fetched source gives these amortisation amounts. Closest independent datapoint: S1 notes Q2 FY26 depreciation & amortisation expenses rose 463.3% YoY and finance costs +70.7% - directionally consistent with heavy capitalisation and only recent catch-up amortisation, but does not confirm the stated totals.
S1: 'borrowings had increased to about RM2.2 billion'. S2: 'Total borrowings stood at RM2.2 billion, up 74.3% from RM1.26 billion a year earlier'.

S1 states borrowings rose 'to about RM2.2 billion from RM160.5 million in 2021'. RM160.5M vs The Edge's RM166.1M - same order of magnitude and same endpoint, but the two numbers differ by ~RM5.6M (possible scope difference: gross debt incl. lease liabilities vs borrowings line). Flag as unexplained variance.
No fetched source reports the FY2022 debt level. S2 provides a different intermediate point: RM1.26b total borrowings at end-Jun 2025.

figures.figure: Net cash +RM63.3M (2020) became net debt RM1.2B (2025)
figures.detail: No source states the 2020 net-cash or 2025 net-debt figures directly. Independent corroboration of the direction and rough magnitude: S2 gives end-Jun-2026 position - cash RM541.6M vs short-term borrowings RM853.1M, total borrowings RM2.2b (implied net debt ~RM1.66b); S2 also gives total borrowings RM1.26b at end-Jun 2025, consistent with a net debt of ~RM1.2b in 2025 after netting cash.

supporting_context_from_independent_sour: S1/S2: FY2025 net profit RM883.85M (+24.9%), revenue RM1.34b (+31.3%) - the 'profit paradox' framing.
S1/S2: JPJ arrears RM314M (May 19-Sep 30 2026 collections), stopped RM231M cheque; confirmed to Bursa as a payable.
S1: MARC Ratings revised MARCWatch to Negative (early Oct) citing insufficient information on the borrowing increase and development-expenditure allocation; warned of rating suspension/withdrawal.
S2/S4: MARC downgraded RM2b sukuk AA-IS -> BB+IS on Oct 18; S3/headlines: second cut toward default level Oct 30.
S2: covenant requires co-founder Wong to remain single largest shareholder; his stake fell to 1.84% via margin-call forced sales.
RSS (headline-level): IFC (World Bank) US$40M for 2.5% stake in Zetrix AI (Feb 2026, Digital News Asia / Malaysian Reserve) - independent confirmation of the AI-Foundation-Lab-linked capital plan.

figures_corroborated_independently: Dev cost = 56% of total assets (MARC via Malaysian Reserve)
figures_with_discrepancy: FY2021 debt: The Edge RM166.1M vs Malaysian Reserve/MARC RM160.5M
figures_single_sourced_not_found: net cash +RM63.3M (2020) and net debt RM1.2B (2025) as exact figures
summary.notes: The two strongest corroborations (S1, S2) both trace their asset-ratio and borrowings data to MARC Ratings' MARCWatch commentary, i.e. MARC is the common upstream source behind both - treat them as two independent newsrooms reporting one independent analyst (MARC), not two fully independent data streams. The amortisation-side claims (RM28.51M/yr, RM139.9M total) are the weakest externally-verified part of the claim; they would need the FY2025 audited financial statements / Bursa annual report PDF, which could not be reached from this environment within the call budget.
